title: Coding-OS Adapter Manifest
description: Schema for src/adapters/<id>/adapter.yaml. Defines an agent adapter — its settings file, hooks directory, path-scoped rules support, and optional default settings deep-merged with aggregated hooks.

id.description: Must match the directory name under adapters/.

settings_file.description: Relative path inside the project where settings.json (or hooks.json) is written.

hooks_dir.description: Relative path inside the project for hook scripts. Null if the adapter has no hooks dir.

rules_dir.description: Relative path for path-scoped rule files. Null if the adapter doesn't support rules.

skills_dir.description: Relative path for skill files. Null if the adapter has no skill system.

commands_dir.description: Relative path for slash-command files (e.g. Claude's .claude/commands). Null for adapters that merge commands into a single instructions file.

entrypoint_file.description: Project-root filename this runtime reads as its instruction entrypoint (e.g. "CLAUDE.md"). cos init/update create it as a relative symlink to AGENTS.md and cos eject removes it, keeping the CLI free of adapter filename literals (rule #11). Null/absent = the runtime reads AGENTS.md directly. Must be a bare filename — no path separators. Spec: docs/playbooks/adapter-authoring.md § The root entrypoint.

sourced_hooks.description: Hook filenames that are sourced (not executed) — doctor skips their exec-bit check.

supports_rules.description: Whether the adapter honours path-scoped rules (YAML frontmatter globs).

supports_settings_json.description: Whether the adapter consumes a JSON settings file.

install_script.description: Relative filename of the adapter install script (usually install.sh).

chat_provider.description: Optional adapter-local Python module that exposes read-only Hub transcript list/get operations.

runtime_entrypoints.description: Provider-neutral adapter-owned runtime modules and capabilities used by supervision. Entrypoints must be bare filenames inside the adapter directory.

presence.description: Module resolving where this runtime stores its transcripts. Narrower than `transcript`, which also reads them: the kernel needs the path to detect an active chat, and importing the adapter's SDK to get it violates P8.

chat.description: Module implementing the Hub chat port: list_sessions, get_session_info, get_session_messages, stream_turn. Core calls these names, never a provider SDK's own surface.

cli_binary.description: Executable name discoverable on PATH for this agent (e.g. "claude"). Consumed by src/cli/doctor.py::_probe_agent_sdk so that file stays free of hardcoded adapter literals (rule #11). Optional — defaults to the adapter id when missing.

sdk_package.description: Importable Python package whose installed version doctor reports for this adapter (e.g. "claude-agent-sdk"). Empty string = no SDK to probe.

sdk_optional_extra.description: Optional-dependency group that installs sdk_package. When set, a missing SDK is a warning because the adapter may retain a CLI fallback.

auth_env_vars.description: Provider authentication environment variables reported by the generic SDK doctor. CLI-managed login may also be valid.

default_settings.description: Adapter-owned defaults deep-merged with aggregated world.hooks by render_settings_json().

hook_registry_output.description: Relative filename within src/adapters/<id>/ where src/cli/hook_renderer.py writes the rendered template (e.g. settings.template.json for claude, hooks.template.json for codex). Null if this adapter does not consume the hook registry.

runtime_env_markers.description: Environment variables whose presence identifies this adapter's runtime. Consumed by src/cli/board_commands.py::_detect_agent_runtime to attribute task_status_history.agent_session — avoids hardcoded adapter-name literals in CLI code (rule #11).

runtime_session_marker.description: Per-panel session identity contract — declares how src/core/hooks/cos-env.sh::_cos_resolve_panel_id and cos_panel_upgrade_from_payload derive the per-panel id from this agent's runtime. Data-driven (Rule 11); adding a new adapter (e.g. gemini) requires only this block + the adapter dir — zero code change in src/core/. Pairs with docs/engineering/state-files.md § Panel-id resolution.

stdin_field.description: JSON key in the hook stdin payload carrying the per-panel session id (typically 'session_id' or 'sessionId' depending on the agent runtime).

env_vars.description: Priority-ordered fallback env vars (probed when stdin is unavailable, e.g. for raw shell tests or hooks that don't slurp stdin). The first non-empty one wins.

hook_capabilities.description: Which {event, matcher} pairs this adapter can actually trigger. Drives src/cli/hook_renderer.py when rendering adapter-specific settings from src/core/hooks/registry.yaml. Key = event name (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit).

matchers.description: Matcher strings this adapter can dispatch for the event. Empty-string matcher ('') means the event fires without a matcher (e.g. Stop).

cursor_native_hooks.description: Cursor-only native hook keys (camelCase, e.g. preCompact) merged into hooks.cursor.template.json after registry render.

script.description: Hook script basename under the adapter hooks dir (same as hook_dispatchers.script).

hook_dispatchers.description: Optional adapter-specific coalescing rules that replace multiple registry-derived hooks for one {event, matcher} pair with a single dispatcher script.

mcp_helper.description: Optional helper script (relative to src/adapters/<id>/) used by src/cli/main.py when wiring the MCP launch config for this agent. Absent means no helper is needed.

mcp_launch.description: Data-driven metadata for src/cli/doctor.py::_load_coding_os_mcp_launch. Lets the C15 check locate and parse the per-agent MCP config without hardcoded adapter-name literals.

loader.description: Which parser in src/cli/doctor.py handles this adapter's MCP config format.

presence.description: Optional Hub board + presence documentation. src/core/board_os/hub_adapter_manifest.py reads hub_glyph/hub_color; signal and presence_events are documentation for adapter-parity.

signal.description: Presence JSON under .coding-os/<adapter>/sessions/ is driven by agent-presence.sh on hook lifecycle events.

presence_events.description: Which events refresh presence for this adapter (documentation only).

hub_glyph.description: Short badge text in Hub Scrumban live-agents strip.

hub_color.description: Badge accent color (hex) for Hub UI.

runtime.description: Hub chat execution capability: 'in_process' = runnable via the agent's SDK inside Hub chat (Claude today); 'roadmap' = declared but not yet runnable. Consumed by src/core/web/routes/config.py::config_adapters for the adapter-grouped model picker.

models.description: Model catalog this adapter offers — drives the Hub pickers and supervision write-time validation. Empty means either a roadmap adapter or a runtime that forwards any model string; core never fabricates IDs (P7), so an empty catalog accepts any non-empty string and the Hub renders a free-text field.

id.description: Model identifier passed to the agent runtime.

label.description: Human-facing model name shown in the picker.

default.description: Whether this is the adapter's default model. At most one per adapter.

bucket.description: Provider rate-limit pool this model draws from. Models sharing a pool share one capacity cooldown; models in different pools stay independent when one is limited. Absent = the adapter is treated as a single pool.

efforts.description: Reasoning-effort levels this adapter's SDK accepts (Claude EffortLevel = low|medium|high|xhigh|max), surfaced in the Hub chat composer. Empty/absent = no effort control for this adapter.

default_effort.description: Pre-selected effort level in the Hub chat composer (must be one of `efforts`).

chat_status.description: Hub chat live-status vocabulary, read per adapter by the composer (no frontend hardcoding — Codex declares its own). Surfaces a friendly 'working…' label while a turn streams.

tool_labels.description: Runtime tool name -> friendly present-participle status verb (e.g. Read -> Reading).

idle_phrases.description: Playful phrases rotated while the agent works without a concrete tool active.

dispatch_timeout_s.description: Wall-clock budget in seconds for one dispatch to this adapter. Omit to use the role/agent default, which is calibrated on the fastest runtime. Declare it when the runtime is materially slower: a successful codex review measured 123s against a 120s agent default and timed out at the finish line.
